name: Learn a second swimming stroke
blurb: Breaststroke or backstroke as a second gear. Having a stroke you can swim slowly and breathe freely in changes swimming from exercise into something you can do for an hour.
steps: For breaststroke, learn the timing above all: pull, breathe, kick, glide — and the glide is the part everyone drops.
Learn the whip kick with feet flexed and turned out; a scissor kick is the common fault and it is much slower.
For backstroke, keep your head still and your ears in the water, rotating the shoulders while the head stays put.
Learn to swim straight on your back by watching the ceiling or lane ropes in your peripheral vision.
Practise one length of drill for every length of full stroke.
Alternate strokes within a session, which builds endurance without overloading one movement pattern.
tips: Breaststroke knee pain usually means your kick is too wide. Narrow it.
The glide is free distance. Rushing the stroke rate makes you slower, not faster.
proof: You swim 200 metres of your second stroke with correct timing, comfortably.
